title: Storage, Filesystems, and Kernel Internals
description: Persistence after virtualization: blocks, inodes, journals, drivers, and the namespaces containers actually use.

sourceReferences.title: xv6 book
sourceReferences.notes: File system after locks. Crash consistency is the hard part.

sourceReferences.title: MIT 6.1810
sourceReferences.notes: Labs add sophisticated VM and networking onto a known kernel.

modules.title: Filesystems
learningObjectives: Treat a filename as a pointer to an inode
Write intent before applying it to the home location

modules.title: I/O path
learningObjectives: Keep recently used blocks in RAM
Let a device move bytes while the CPU does other work

modules.title: Modern isolation extras
learningObjectives: Restrict what a process can see of the machine
Compose namespaces and limits without inventing a new kernel

concepts.name: Block devices
concepts.summary: Fixed-size sectors and the fiction of a linear disk.
objectives: Describe a block device as a linear array of fixed-size sectors
Predict why the filesystem, not the program, chooses which sector to write

concepts.name: Inodes
concepts.summary: The on-disk object a filename eventually names.
objectives: Describe an inode as the on-disk object a filename eventually names
Distinguish the inode's metadata and data blocks from the name that points at it

concepts.name: Directories
concepts.summary: A list of names to inode numbers.
objectives: Describe a directory as a list of names to inode numbers
Predict what two names for one inode means

concepts.name: Filesystem layout
concepts.summary: Superblock, bitmaps, and where the data lives.
objectives: Locate superblock, free-space map, inodes, and data on a disk image
Predict what is lost if the free-space map is wrong after a crash

concepts.name: Journaling
concepts.summary: Write the intent before the damage.
objectives: Describe journaling as writing the intent before applying it to the home location
Predict why the journal must hit disk before the metadata it describes

concepts.name: Crash consistency
concepts.summary: A power cut in the middle of rename.
objectives: Diagnose a filesystem after a power cut in the middle of rename
Predict which states a journaled rename may legally show after replay

concepts.name: The VFS
concepts.summary: One API over many filesystem types.
objectives: Describe the VFS as one API over many filesystem types
Predict why two mounts can implement the same open/read/write differently

concepts.name: Mounts
concepts.summary: Grafting a tree onto a directory.
objectives: Describe a mount as grafting another tree onto a directory
Predict which filesystem serves a path after a mount covers that directory

concepts.name: Buffer cache
concepts.summary: Recently used blocks kept in RAM.
objectives: Describe the buffer cache as recently used blocks kept in RAM
Predict why a write that hits the cache is not yet durable

concepts.name: Page cache
concepts.summary: File contents as pages, not just blocks.
objectives: Describe the page cache as file contents kept as pages, not just device blocks
Contrast a page-cache hit on a mapped file with a block read from the device

concepts.name: DMA
concepts.summary: The device writes memory while the CPU does something else.
objectives: Describe DMA as the device writing memory while the CPU does other work
Predict why the CPU must not use a buffer until the device says the transfer is done

concepts.name: Device drivers
concepts.summary: The kernel code that speaks a particular device's dialect.
objectives: Describe a driver as kernel code that speaks one device's dialect
Predict what the rest of the kernel sees after the driver hides the device registers

concepts.name: Virtio
concepts.summary: A device model designed to be virtualized.
objectives: Describe virtio as a device model designed to be emulated or paravirtualized
Predict why a guest driver talking virtio is cheaper than emulating a real NIC

concepts.name: init and userspace bring-up
concepts.summary: The first process and everything it starts.
objectives: Describe init as the first user process that starts everything else
Predict what happens to the machine if init exits

concepts.name: Namespaces
concepts.summary: A process that cannot see the whole machine.
objectives: Describe a namespace as a process that cannot see the whole machine
Predict what a process in a PID namespace believes is process 1

concepts.name: Linux namespace types
concepts.summary: PID, mount, net, user — different lies.
objectives: Distinguish PID, mount, net, and user namespaces as different restricted views
Predict which namespace hides the host's network interfaces

concepts.name: cgroups
concepts.summary: Accounting and limits on CPU, memory, I/O.
objectives: Describe a cgroup as accounting and limits on CPU, memory, and I/O
Predict what happens when a group hits its memory limit

concepts.name: Capabilities
concepts.summary: Splitting root into bits you can drop.
objectives: Describe capabilities as splitting root into bits you can drop
Predict a denial when a process has dropped the bit a privileged operation needs

concepts.name: seccomp
concepts.summary: A filter on which syscalls remain legal.
objectives: Describe seccomp as a filter on which syscalls remain legal
Predict why an allowed open can still be a sandbox hole

concepts.name: Reducing the syscall surface
concepts.summary: Why a sandboxed process still needs open(2).
objectives: Explain why a sandboxed process still needs a few syscalls to do useful work
Predict the tradeoff between a tiny syscall surface and a working program

concepts.name: KVM at a glance
concepts.summary: The kernel as a hypervisor for other kernels.
objectives: Describe KVM as the host kernel running other kernels in a less-privileged mode
Predict what a privileged instruction in the guest causes on the host

concepts.name: Containers
concepts.summary: Namespaces plus cgroups plus a filesystem view — not a VM.
objectives: Describe a container as namespaces plus cgroups plus a filesystem view
Contrast a container with a virtual machine that has its own kernel
